readerTitle: Why asking for one introduction beats paying for ten
caseNote: 가상 사례 2개 (회계 사무소, 대기업 내부 데이터팀) + 실제 연구 (독일 은행 추천 프로그램, Schmitt 외 2011) + 가상 적용 (건축 사무소용 소프트웨어)
insight: 추천하는 사람이 치르는 진짜 비용은 수고와 평판 위험이다. 보상을 키우기보다 그 비용을 줄여 주면 추천이 늘어난다.
misconception: 추천이 안 들어오는 건 보상이 작아서다. 추천 보상금을 올리면 추천도 늘어난다.

sources.text: Schmitt, P., Skiera, B., & Van den Bulte, C. (2011). Referral Programs and Customer Value. Journal of Marketing, 75(1), 46–59.
회계 사무소, 내부 데이터팀, 건축 사무소용 소프트웨어 사례와 차트 수치는 모두 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: Schmitt 외(2011) 연구: 독일 은행에서 추천으로 들어온 고객이 이탈률이 낮고 장기 가치가 더 높았다는 결론을 확인하세요. 구체적 퍼센트(약 16~18% 수준으로 기억됨)는 원문 확인 전이라 카드에 넣지 않고 일반적 표현으로만 썼습니다.
3번 카드 차트 수치(6개월 추천 건수 2건 vs 11건)는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 카드에 illustrative 표시가 있습니다.
7번 카드의 '일부 업종은 추천 보상을 제한한다'는 일반적 서술입니다. 특정 국가·업종의 법률 조언으로 읽히지 않도록 구체적 규정은 넣지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Why asking for one introduction beats paying for ten
body: A bookkeeping firm offered clients $500 for every new client they sent. Six months later, two had come in.
Across town, a data team inside a big retailer offered nothing at all. Its tool spread to eleven new departments, almost all through introductions from people already using it.

image.label: Two offices: one with a cash reward sign, one with people shaking hands
image.brief: 화면을 좌우로 나눈 일러스트. 왼쪽은 작은 회계 사무소 벽에 "$500 per referral" 포스터가 붙어 있지만 조용함. 오른쪽은 대기업 사무실에서 한 직원이 동료 두 명을 서로 소개하며 악수시키는 장면. 실제 회사 로고 없음.

cards.title: Your clients love you. You want more like them.
body: You run a 12-person bookkeeping firm for small manufacturers. Clients rate you highly, but new business comes in slowly.
You want your happy clients to send you others like them. What do you try first?

options.text: Offer $500 cash for every referred client who signs
options.feedback: A reward can help, but it doesn't remove what holds people back: the effort of making an intro and the worry of vouching for you. Some clients may also feel it makes their recommendation look bought.

options.text: Right after a smooth year-end close, ask each client for one specific introduction and offer to draft the email
options.feedback: You ask when they feel the value most, name who you want, and do the work for them. It costs time, not cash, and it's harder to scale.

options.text: Add a "Refer a friend" line to every invoice
options.feedback: Cheap and constant, but easy to ignore. A general request on a bill asks nothing specific and arrives at the moment clients think about cost, not value.

cards.title: Same goal, very different results.
body: The firm offered money and waited. The data team did something smaller: whenever a manager said the tool had saved their week, the team asked, "Who else in finance has this problem?" Then it wrote the intro message for them.

groups.label: New customers from referrals in six months

rows.label: Data team: specific ask, no reward

cards.title: Referrals
body: A **referral** is a recommendation you deliberately ask for, make easy to give, and can trace back to the person who gave it.

Word of mouth happens on its own. A referral is designed. And every referral has a hidden price: the person making it **lends you their reputation**. If you disappoint the new customer, they look bad too.

image.label: A person handing over a card with their own face on it
image.brief: 한 사람이 다른 사람에게 명함을 건네는데, 명함에 회사 이름이 아니라 건네는 사람 자신의 얼굴이 그려져 있음. '추천은 내 평판을 빌려주는 것'이라는 은유. 따뜻한 색감, 로고 없음.

cards.title: Lower what the referrer pays.
body: People who like you still hold back for three reasons: it takes effort, it feels awkward, and it risks their reputation. Good referral asks shrink all three.
list: **Timing:** ask right after a clear win, when the value is fresh
**Specific ask:** name the kind of person, not "anyone you know"
**Ready-made intro:** write the message they can forward
**Close the loop:** tell them how it went, so they feel safe doing it again
cards.callout: The data team never paid anyone. It made saying yes easy and safe.

cards.title: Referred customers often stay longer.
body: Researchers studied a German bank's referral program and tracked thousands of customers. Those who came through referrals were more likely to stay and were worth more over time than customers won other ways.
One likely reason: referrers screen for fit. They tend to recommend you to people who resemble them, and they already know you work well for people like them.
cards.softwareNote: In software, referred users often activate faster because a colleague already showed them what the product is for. Tracking referral links lets you compare their retention with users from ads.

cards.title: Referrals amplify. They don't fix.
body: If the work is only average, asking harder just spends your customers' goodwill. Referrals multiply what customers already feel.
They also stay inside your customers' circles. That can make it hard to reach a new market.
And large rewards can attract people who refer for the money, not the fit. In some industries, paying for referrals is also restricted, so check before you offer cash.

cards.title: Now it's software for architects.
body: You sell project-tracking software to small architecture firms. Users who finish their first project in it tend to love it. You want more referrals. Which plan fits best?

options.text: Show a pop-up on day one asking new users to invite five colleagues
options.feedback: Fast and automatic, but users haven't seen any value yet. You'd be asking them to vouch for something they barely know.

options.text: When a project closes, prompt: "Know another firm drowning in spreadsheets?" with a pre-written note
options.feedback: You ask at the moment of success, describe exactly who to refer, and remove the writing effort. Fewer prompts, but each lands better.

options.text: Give one free month to anyone whose referral signs up
options.feedback: A fair thank-you that may tip a few people. But without a good moment and an easy message, most happy users still won't get around to it.

cards.title: Make recommending you easy and safe.
body: A referral costs the referrer effort and reputation. Lower those costs with good timing, a specific ask and a ready-made intro before you reach for bigger rewards.
**Try it today:** think of one customer who just had a clear win with you. Ask them for one specific introduction, and offer to write the message.
